newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says he is flexible on taxes, Medicaid.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says he is flexible on taxes, Medicaid.

text.p: President Clinton said in an interview published Thursday that he is willing to be flexible in dealing with the Republican-led Congress on Medicare, tax cuts and other issues.

In an interview with New York television station WBIS+, Clinton suggested that a budget deal may be reached and called for a bipartisan commission to study reforms in Medicare and Social Security with a report due by mid-1997.
He said he would be flexible on a capital gains tax cut. "I've never been philosophically opposed as some of my fellow Democrats are," he said.
But Clinton said he was against making a capital gains cut retroactive and that the loss of revenue from any cut would have to be made up elsewhere.

Clinton said he disagreed with Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan's concern over rising wages causing an increase in inflation. "You haven't seen any kind of demands that people would say are outrageous, even in tight labour markets," Clinton said.

Clinton also indicated that he might support raising the retirement age as part of a reform package for Social Security and making the wealthy elderly people pay more for Medicare. "I'm not necessarily opposed to that," he said about proposals to boost Medicare payments.
